title: There is no such things as 'AI Ethics'
author: Paul Matthews
summary: Paul Matthews opens with a school leader who says his school is lost at sea with AI, and answers that school leaders are more prepared than they realise. His provocative claim is that there is no such thing as AI ethics, because ChatGPT did not bring any new moral principles with it and existing values, mission and vision are what schools need to navigate it. He tests the claim against the Australian Framework for Generative AI in Schools, whose six principles are ones schools held long before 2022. He then draws on Aristotle's phronesis, or practical wisdom, to describe ethics applied in context, which grows with practice and from wise people rather than from new rules. The practical upshot is that schools should look to their own heritage and values as a working compass, and he promises a follow-up exercise for applying those values to AI with a leadership team, staff or students.
points: Matthews reframes AI governance in schools as an application problem, not a principles problem, because new situations call for old ethics wisely applied.
He uses the Australian AFGAIS framework as a worked example, noting its six principles are the same values schools already held in 1926.
Aristotle's phronesis is offered as the missing skill, practical wisdom about what to do with these people in this situation right now.
The message to anxious school leaders is that their school's existing values and history are a working compass, so they are not starting from zero.
quotes: But when ChatGPT launched in 2022, it didn’t bring any new ethics with it. In fact, all the same moral principles we held to before still apply.
Our values, mission, and vision are not in need of an update in light of AI. They are precisely what we need to navigate AI wisely.
New situations don’t require new ethics, they need old ethics wisely applied.
Was there a single school not committed to these values before 2022? These are the same values schools held in 1926, and still hold to in 2026.
Phronesis is practical wisdom. It’s knowing the right thing to do, in this situation, with these people, right now.
Schools don’t need new ethical principles to navigate AI. They simply need their old principles to be applied to a new situation.
